messages.content:
thumbd is moving to containers, and the deployment there sets configuration through
environment variables instead of editing config files. Please teach thumbconf to read
them:

- a setting section.key can be set by the variable THUMBD_SECTION_KEY (upper case, so
  server.port is THUMBD_SERVER_PORT and storage.timeout_s is THUMBD_STORAGE_TIMEOUT_S).
  A variable wins over the configuration file, and the file wins over the default.
  load_config should read os.environ, or the mapping passed as a new environ argument
  when there is one, and the show, get, and check commands should use the variables;
- variables are text, so convert them to the kind of the setting: integers and floats
  as numbers; booleans from true/false, yes/no, on/off, or 1/0 in any case, with spaces
  around them ignored; lists as comma-separated items (an empty value is an empty
  list); a string as it is. Then apply the same limits as for a value in the file;
- a variable that cannot be converted or breaks a limit raises ConfigError with a
  message that names the variable, and every command prints it and exits with status 2,
  like a bad value in the file;
- the platform's deployment templates still set the older names listed in
  config/env-aliases.toml (that table belongs to the platform team, so do not edit it).
  Support those names too, for the setting each is mapped to, read from the alias table
  that sits next to the configuration file. If a THUMBD_ variable and an older name are
  both set for a setting, the THUMBD_ variable wins.

Everything else should keep working as it does now: with no variables set, the library
and the commands behave as before, including the messages for a bad configuration file.
